sources.title: E. Wiedemann (ed. J. Skipper), Lecture Notes: Navier-Stokes Equations (Universität Ulm, WS 2018/19)
sources.locator: Chapter 1 Sections 1.1-1.3; Chapter 2 Sections 2.1-2.4; Chapter 3 Sections 3.1-3.2; Chapter 4 Sections 4.1-4.5; Chapter 5 (read for scope only)

contents.name: Section 1.1 physical derivation of the Navier-Stokes equations
contents.reason: Physical derivation and modelling motivation; this page is mathematics and adopts no physical postulates or constitutive reading of the equations.

contents.name: Section 1.2 elementary mathematical properties and the energy balance
contents.support: The L2 energy identity and the vanishing of the transport term after integration by parts follow the presentation here; the item reproves them on the torus in coefficient form.

contents.name: Section 1.3 related models (inviscid limit, compressible and non-Newtonian fluids)
contents.reason: Only the incompressible constant-density system with constant viscosity is treated; compressible and non-Newtonian constitutive laws are separate modelling subjects.

contents.name: Definitions 2.1-2.2: Fourier characterisation of H^s(T^3), Plancherel and homogeneous Sobolev spaces
contents.support: The coefficient norms, weight conventions and the reality condition follow this characterisation; the page fixes the normalization explicitly and cites the published torus Fourier basis theorem for parseval.

contents.name: Lemma 2.4 and Theorem 2.6: weakly divergence-free fields and the Helmholtz decomposition of the torus
contents.support: The divergence-free subspace and the orthogonal decomposition u=Pu+nabla f with explicit multiplier k⊗k/|k|^2 are stated and derived coefficientwise in the definition item.

contents.name: Definition 2.7 and Lemma 2.8: the Leray projection and its commutation with derivatives
contents.support: The projection, self-adjointness, contractivity and commutation with Lambda^s, partial_j and Delta are part of the definition item and are used throughout the page.

contents.name: Definition 3.1 and Sections 3.1.1-3.1.2: the Galerkin approximation and its finite system of ODEs
contents.support: The N-th order Galerkin system on the Fourier modes, its finite-dimensional state space and the resulting locally Lipschitz ODE are reproduced with explicit invariance and maximal-solution statements.

contents.name: Chapter 4 Section 4.1: Bochner spaces and integration of curves
contents.support: The page replaces Bochner theory by a self-contained Riemann-sum integral with the fundamental theorem for continuous curves in the complete H^m spaces.

contents.name: Theorem 4.14: existence of strong solutions with T=C||u_0||_{L2}^{-4} via Agmon's inequality
contents.reason: The page proves local existence for smooth H^s data by the commutator route with lifespan (2C_s||u_0||_{H^s})^{-1}; the L2-based Agmon route of this theorem is a different theorem with a different data class and is not rebuilt here.

contents.name: Lemma 4.13 Agmon's inequality via low/high frequency splitting
contents.reason: The page's estimates bound gradients by the H^s norm through the Sobolev embedding instead; Agmon's L-infinity interpolation is not needed and is not asserted.

contents.name: Chapter 4 Section 4.2: properties of strong solutions and the H^m energy inequality
contents.support: The H^m energy identity, the role of the transport term and the differential inequality leading to the common lifespan follow this section, with the commutator estimate supplied by lem-tame-transport-commutator.

contents.name: Theorem 4.16: higher regularity and uniform H^m bounds for the Galerkin approximations
contents.support: The induction giving uniform-in-N bounds in every H^m on the fixed base interval is reproduced with the explicit exponential constants.

contents.name: Theorems 4.17-4.18: spatial and time regularity of strong solutions
contents.support: The page proves joint C-infinity of a strong solution directly by the product rule for bilinear maps and the Sobolev embedding, which supplies the same conclusion on the torus.

contents.name: Section 4.5 blow-up and the Beale-Kato-Majda criterion
contents.reason: No continuation criterion is proved; the known open global regularity problem is recorded honestly in rem-local-versus-known-open-global-fluid-scope without being claimed as a theorem.

contents.name: Chapter 5: the vanishing-viscosity limit
contents.reason: The inviscid limit and boundary-layer analysis are distinct research subjects not treated by this page's local well-posedness items.

sources.title: A. J. Majda and A. L. Bertozzi, Vorticity and Incompressible Flow (Cambridge Texts in Applied Mathematics, CUP 2002)
sources.locator: Chapter 1 Sections 1.1-1.9 (equations, exact solutions, conserved quantities, Leray's formulation, Fourier series and Hodge decomposition); Chapter 3 Sections 3.1-3.3 (energy methods, local-in-time existence, vorticity criteria); Chapter 4 Sections 4.1 and 4.4 (particle-trajectory existence and higher regularity)

contents.name: Section 1.1 equations (1.1)-(1.3) and the periodic setting (1.8)
contents.support: The pair of model equations on the torus and the pressure-free projection convention are exactly the object of the main theorem; the page fixes signs and normalization explicitly.

contents.name: Sections 1.4-1.6 exact solutions and vorticity transport
contents.support: The transverse plane waves, shear flows and the Taylor-Green steady state verified on the companion page are the torus instances of the exact solutions presented here.

contents.name: Section 1.7 conserved quantities of ideal and viscous flows (Propositions 1.12-1.14)
contents.reason: No conservation theorem for vorticity integrals, helicity or impulse is authored on this page; those results would need their own items and convergence hypotheses.

contents.name: Section 1.8 Leray's formulation, equation (1.84), Lemma 1.6 and Proposition 1.15
contents.support: The pressure recovery -Delta p = tr(nabla v)^2 and the elimination of the pressure are the content of the reconstruction item, with the coefficient formula and its smoothness proved explicitly on the torus.

contents.name: Subsection 1.9.1 Fourier series conventions (1.99)-(1.102) and Section 1.9.2 elliptic facts
contents.support: The coefficient convention, Plancherel identity and the differentiation rule for coefficients agree with the page's conventions; the published torus Fourier basis theorem remains the primary supplier.

contents.name: Proposition 1.18 Hodge decomposition of the torus and display (1.98)
contents.support: The multiplier k⊗k/|k|^2 and the orthogonal decomposition of a field into divergence-free and gradient parts are the definition item's projection statement.

contents.name: Section 3.2.1 Lemma 3.4 calculus inequalities in Sobolev spaces (products and commutators)
contents.support: The product bounds and the Banach-algebra property for H^s with s>3/2 are reproduced with discrete Young inequality and Cauchy-Schwarz constants on the lattice.

contents.name: Lemma 3.4 estimate (3.32): the commutator calculus inequality
contents.support: The tame commutator bound [Lambda^m,u·nabla]u is proved coefficientwise with explicit constants, following the structure of this inequality.

contents.name: Subsection 3.2.2 global existence for the mollified regularization (Theorem 3.2, Proposition 3.6)
contents.reason: The page uses the Fourier-mode Galerkin approximation instead of mollification; the regularized-equation construction is an alternative route that is not reproduced.

contents.name: Subsection 3.2.3 Theorem 3.4 local-in-time existence, estimate (3.59) and Corollary 3.2
contents.support: Local existence with a lifespan controlled by the initial high norm, the uniform H^m and time-derivative bounds and the maximal-time dichotomy follow this theorem, adapted to the periodic Galerkin setting.

contents.name: Proposition 3.1 and Corollary 3.1 basic energy estimates and uniqueness
contents.support: The difference energy estimate, Gronwall argument and uniqueness of smooth solutions are the content of the uniqueness and stability theorem.

contents.name: Lemma 3.8 interpolation in Sobolev spaces
contents.support: The interpolation inequality bounding the intermediate norm is proved directly by Holder's inequality on the weighted coefficient family and used for the H^{s-1} stability estimate.

contents.name: Section 3.3 accumulation of vorticity and global existence criteria (Corollary 3.2)
contents.reason: Vorticity-based global criteria are not proved; the page records the open global problem and proves no continuation criterion beyond the elementary H^s restarting argument.

contents.name: Section 4.1 local existence via the particle-trajectory method
contents.reason: The Lagrangian particle-trajectory construction is an alternative existence proof not used here; the page's route is the Eulerian Galerkin estimate.

contents.name: Section 4.4 higher regularity
contents.support: The higher-regularity upgrade is supplied by the page's own bootstrap via the product rule for bilinear maps rather than by the elliptic arguments of this section.

sources.title: R. S. Laugesen, Harmonic Analysis Lecture Notes (arXiv:0903.3845, version of May 2017)
sources.locator: Chapters 1-2 (Fourier coefficients, smoothness versus decay, summability and the failure of absolute convergence for general L^2 data) and Chapter 5 (the Wiener algebra and absolutely summable coefficients on the circle)

contents.name: Chapter 1 Theorems 1.6-1.8: smoothness implies decay of Fourier coefficients and the converse bounds
contents.support: The contrast between decay and absolute summability is the phenomenon the counterexample records at order zero on the torus; the witness family is constructed explicitly on the lattice.

contents.name: Chapter 2 summability kernels, Fejer kernel and uniqueness of Fourier coefficients
contents.support: The uniqueness argument for the continuous representative is proved on the torus from the published basis theorem and Stone-Weierstrass; the kernel-based uniqueness in these notes gives the classical counterpart on the circle.

contents.name: Chapter 5 absolute convergence and the Wiener algebra
contents.support: The positive result that absolutely summable coefficients give continuous sums corresponds to the torus embedding for sigma>3/2 proved in the item; the notes supply the one-dimensional model.
